summary: All 24 backend tests passed. Google Sign-in endpoints (POST /api/auth/google/session, GET /api/auth/me, POST /api/auth/logout) work correctly. Existing JWT auth (register/login/users-me) still works and is dual-supported by /api/auth/me. Admin user_id backfill verified. MongoDB indexes (users.email unique, users.user_id unique, user_sessions.session_token unique, user_sessions.expires_at TTL) all present.

minor.issue: Emergent auth network/timeout errors raise 500 which could leak details. Fine for now, but consider mapping upstream 5xx to a generic 502.
Returns success even when Authorization header is missing or token is fake. Acceptable idempotent behavior but does not signal to client whether an actual session was deleted.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 748 lines - consider splitting into routers (auth, users, messages, recipients, subscriptions, admin) for maintainability.
google_session upserts user without setting `last_checkin`/`updated_at` for existing users beyond picture — check-in streak logic could ignore Google users' recent activity.

Uses datetime.utcnow() (naive) in most places but datetime.now(timezone.utc) for sessions. Session expiry comparison relies on normalization at read-time — fine, but consistency would prevent subtle timezone bugs.
SECRET_KEY has a hardcoded fallback default. Should require env var and fail-fast if unset in production.
get_current_user tries session_token lookup on EVERY request even for JWT tokens (adds a DB round-trip). Consider a quick prefix/format check or cache.
seed_data_creation: Created one TEST_user_<uuid>@example.com during registration test; cleanup fixture removes all TEST_user_* records after the run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend suite at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py exercises JWT auth, Google session endpoints (invalid path only — real Google OAuth flow requires an actual session_id from Emergent redirect), all existing endpoints, and Mongo indexes. Uses EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL from frontend/.env (falls back to EXPO_BACKEND_URL). Note: real Google session validation cannot be tested via API — only the 401/400 rejection paths were exercised.
